/decision-hub.headline: How should a five-person team choose software without a technical administrator?
/decision-hub.decisionContext: Start with the team’s outcome, constraints, and evidence gaps before comparing any software approach.

blocks.title: Start with the decision
blocks.summary: Define the software decision before evaluating a category or product.

claims.statement: Define the software decision before evaluating a category or product.

blocks.title: Why this is different
blocks.summary: A small team without technical administration carries different operational risk.

claims.statement: A small team without technical administration carries different operational risk.

blocks.title: Name the outcome
blocks.summary: Describe the work outcome the software must help the team achieve.

claims.statement: Describe the work outcome the software must help the team achieve.

blocks.title: See the full problem
blocks.summary: Include adoption, ownership, support, security, and change effort in the decision.

claims.statement: Include adoption, ownership, support, security, and change effort in the decision.

blocks.title: Separate symptoms from causes
blocks.summary: Identify the recurring friction that a software choice should address.

claims.statement: Identify the recurring friction that a software choice should address.

blocks.title: Ask the context questions
blocks.summary: Clarify who will operate the tool, how soon it is needed, and what must remain simple.

claims.statement: Clarify who will operate the tool, how soon it is needed, and what must remain simple.

blocks.title: Ask the domain questions
blocks.summary: Identify the workflow, integrations, data, and support questions that apply.

claims.statement: Identify the workflow, integrations, data, and support questions that apply.

blocks.title: Choose criteria deliberately
blocks.summary: Use criteria that reflect the team’s operating limits rather than generic popularity.

claims.statement: Use criteria that reflect the team’s operating limits rather than generic popularity.

blocks.title: Make trade-offs visible
blocks.summary: State what the team gives up when it prioritises speed, control, flexibility, or support.

claims.statement: State what the team gives up when it prioritises speed, control, flexibility, or support.

blocks.title: Follow the right path
blocks.summary: Route the team by its constraints instead of declaring a universal winner.

claims.statement: Route the team by its constraints instead of declaring a universal winner.

blocks.title: Check the evidence
blocks.summary: Keep evidence state and review date visible so later research can update the record.

claims.statement: Keep evidence state and review date visible so later research can update the record.

blocks.title: Continue to solution approaches
blocks.summary: Use the solution guide to turn the criteria into conditional software approaches.

claims.statement: Use the solution guide to turn the criteria into conditional software approaches.

/solution-hub.headline: Which software approach fits a five-person team that cannot maintain its own systems?
/solution-hub.decisionContext: Use the same constraints to compare approaches conditionally, not to publish a universal vendor ranking.

blocks.title: Start with the team’s goal
blocks.summary: Define the practical outcome the five-person team needs from its software.

claims.statement: Define the practical outcome the five-person team needs from its software.

blocks.title: Describe the operating situation
blocks.summary: Keep the lack of a technical administrator and limited implementation capacity explicit.

claims.statement: Keep the lack of a technical administrator and limited implementation capacity explicit.

blocks.title: Use decision criteria
blocks.summary: Prioritise criteria that make ownership, onboarding, support, and daily operation manageable.

claims.statement: Prioritise criteria that make ownership, onboarding, support, and daily operation manageable.

blocks.title: Group by fit scenario
blocks.summary: Choose an approach only where its operating demands match the team’s stated constraints.

claims.statement: Choose an approach only where its operating demands match the team’s stated constraints.

blocks.title: Explain the fit
blocks.summary: Show why an approach may fit one situation and not another.

claims.statement: Show why an approach may fit one situation and not another.

blocks.title: Show what supports the path
blocks.summary: Present the evidence state and review date instead of treating incomplete research as certainty.

claims.statement: Present the evidence state and review date instead of treating incomplete research as certainty.

blocks.title: Resolve the concrete scenario
blocks.summary: Continue to the five-person scenario to test the approach against fixed constraints.

claims.statement: Continue to the five-person scenario to test the approach against fixed constraints.

motionBrief.reducedMotion: No comparison or conclusion depends on animation.

/scenarios.headline: For a five-person team with no technical administrator, what should guide the next software choice?
/scenarios.decisionContext: This is a worked decision frame, not a product comparison or a promise of a particular result.

blocks.title: Define the situation
blocks.summary: A five-person team needs software without a dedicated technical administrator.

claims.statement: A five-person team needs software without a dedicated technical administrator.

blocks.title: State assumptions
blocks.summary: Treat team size, operating capacity, and implementation time as assumptions to revisit.

claims.statement: Treat team size, operating capacity, and implementation time as assumptions to revisit.

blocks.title: Set hard constraints
blocks.summary: Exclude paths that require ongoing specialist administration or unsupported operational effort.

claims.statement: Exclude paths that require ongoing specialist administration or unsupported operational effort.

blocks.title: Keep viable approaches open
blocks.summary: Consider only approaches that can be operated by the stated team after onboarding.

claims.statement: Consider only approaches that can be operated by the stated team after onboarding.

blocks.title: Explain exclusions
blocks.summary: Record why an approach fails a hard constraint rather than silently removing it.

claims.statement: Record why an approach fails a hard constraint rather than silently removing it.

blocks.title: Use the relevant criteria
blocks.summary: Assess operational ownership, onboarding, support, security, and workflow fit.

claims.statement: Assess operational ownership, onboarding, support, security, and workflow fit.

blocks.title: Tie criteria to evidence
blocks.summary: Keep each conclusion linked to a current evidence state and source record.

claims.statement: Keep each conclusion linked to a current evidence state and source record.

blocks.title: Show the trade-offs
blocks.summary: Make clear how a choice may trade flexibility or control for lower day-to-day operating burden.

claims.statement: Make clear how a choice may trade flexibility or control for lower day-to-day operating burden.

blocks.title: Name what remains unknown
blocks.summary: Do not convert missing product research into a confident recommendation.

claims.statement: Do not convert missing product research into a confident recommendation.

blocks.title: Use conditional verdicts
blocks.summary: Choose a path only if its evidence and operating demands continue to match the team’s situation.

claims.statement: Choose a path only if its evidence and operating demands continue to match the team’s situation.

blocks.title: Choose or avoid with reasons
blocks.summary: Use the stated criteria to explain the next investigation, not to assert a winner.

claims.statement: Use the stated criteria to explain the next investigation, not to assert a winner.

blocks.title: Return to the decision path
blocks.summary: Revisit the decision guide when a constraint or evidence state changes.

claims.statement: Revisit the decision guide when a constraint or evidence state changes.

motionBrief.reducedMotion: The complete scenario remains readable without motion or JavaScript.

presentation.artDirection: A focused constraint-led composition that gives the conditional verdict visual weight.
